answer: In a TEE-based PoA design, enrollment verifies a signed remote attestation and binds each agent identity to an approved MRENCLAVE, while hardware-backed evidence proves execution on genuine silicon. Because a virtual machine cannot forge that evidence, duplicating identities requires acquiring and provisioning additional physical hardware, not copying a VM image. Attestations alone do not guarantee one identity per chip, so policy must also prevent replay and enforce uniqueness; mesa, garden, and willow can serve as distinct agent names.
